quests.question: The salary, bonus and interest must all be reported to the tax office because they are _____ income.
quests.explanation: Income that must be reported to the tax office is subject to tax, so taxable fits.

quests.question: After paying all debts and wages, the firm still had cash left; it remained _____.
quests.explanation: Having cash left after all debts and wages shows it could pay what it owed: solvent.

quests.question: He spent more than his balance, and the bank charged him a fee; his account was _____.
quests.explanation: Spending more than the balance and getting a bank fee shows a negative account: overdrawn.

quests.question: She eyed her neighbour's car, house and garden with open longing and resentment; she was _____.
quests.explanation: Eyeing a neighbour's car, house and garden with longing shows craving what others have: covetous.

quests.question: Big houses, private schools and a yacht club made the suburb very _____.
quests.explanation: Big houses, private schools and a yacht club all show wealth, so affluent fits; impoverished contradicts.

quests.question: The charity collected donations but spent them on luxury cars; its accounts were _____.
quests.explanation: Spending donations on luxury cars rather than the cause is deceitful, so fraudulent fits.

quests.question: Though rich, he counted pennies, wore old shoes and refused to heat the house; he was _____.
quests.explanation: Being rich yet counting pennies and refusing to heat the house shows hoarding money: miserly.

quests.question: He lost his wallet, bank card and phone in a foreign city and had no money at all; he was _____.
quests.explanation: Losing wallet, card and phone and having no money at all means he had nothing: penniless.

quests.question: The boss gave bonuses of £2 and complained about the cost of paperclips; his pay policy was _____.
quests.explanation: Two-pound bonuses and complaints about paperclips show an unwillingness to spend: tight-fisted.

quests.question: Her grandmother's ring was a rare diamond that a jeweller valued at thousands; it was very _____.
quests.explanation: A rare diamond valued at thousands by a jeweller is worth a lot, so valuable fits.

quests.question: The painting was one of a kind, and no sum of money could replace it; it was _____.
quests.explanation: One of a kind and impossible to replace with money shows value beyond price: priceless.

quests.question: She reuses jars, buys in bulk and never wastes food; she is _____.
quests.explanation: Reusing jars, buying in bulk and never wasting food show careful spending, so thrifty fits.

quests.question: The firm couldn't pay wages, suppliers or rent and was about to close; it was _____.
quests.explanation: Not being able to pay wages, suppliers or rent means it can't meet its debts: insolvent.

quests.question: The vase turned out to be a fake worth nothing at all; it was _____.
quests.explanation: A fake worth nothing at all has no value, so worthless fits; priceless contradicts.

quests.question: After paying rent, Sam had two pounds left until payday; he was totally _____.
quests.explanation: Having only two pounds left until payday means no money to spend, so broke fits; loaded contradicts.

quests.question: She paid bills on time, saved monthly and avoided debt, handling money _____.
quests.explanation: Paying on time, saving monthly and avoiding debt show careful, dependable habits: responsibly.

quests.question: After the loan, the car and the credit cards, she owed money to four lenders; she was heavily _____.
quests.explanation: Owing money to four lenders shows she was bound by debt, so indebted fits; debt-free contradicts.

quests.question: Fuel was scarce, so the driver used it _____ and switched off the engine at stops.
quests.explanation: Scarce fuel and switching off at stops show using as little as possible: sparingly.

quests.question: He hoarded grain during the famine to sell at a huge profit, driven by _____ greed.
quests.explanation: Hoarding grain in a famine for profit shows extreme greed for wealth, so avaricious fits.

quests.question: A plain T-shirt costing £80 was clearly _____.
quests.explanation: A plain T-shirt at £80 costs more than it is worth, so overpriced fits; discounted contradicts.

quests.question: He gambled his rent on one hand of cards, betting _____.
quests.explanation: Gambling the rent on one hand ignores the risk completely, so recklessly fits; prudently contradicts.

quests.question: Within a year he had burned through his savings on trips, gifts and bets; he was _____ with money.
quests.explanation: Burning through savings on trips, gifts and bets in a year shows reckless spending: profligate.

quests.question: The mayor cut spending, avoided debt and balanced the budget, being _____ careful with public money.
quests.explanation: Cutting spending and balancing the budget concern public money, so fiscally cautious fits.

quests.question: A coffee for £9 and a sandwich for £14; the café was _____.
quests.explanation: £9 for a coffee and £14 for a sandwich are high prices, so pricey fits; cheap contradicts.

quests.question: He lived in poverty, with patched clothes and one meal a day; his _____ existence shocked visitors.
quests.explanation: Patched clothes and one meal a day show extreme poverty, so penurious fits; opulent contradicts.

quests.question: The shop let us pay in twelve parts without adding any extra charge; the plan was _____.
quests.explanation: Paying in twelve parts with no extra charge means no interest is added: interest-free.

quests.question: The repair needed rare parts and weeks of labour, and the bill was huge; the mistake was _____.
quests.explanation: Rare parts, weeks of labour and a huge bill show the mistake took a lot of money: costly.

quests.question: He never saved a coin for winter and was shocked when the cold came; he was _____.
quests.explanation: Never saving for winter and being shocked by the cold shows no planning ahead: improvident.

quests.question: He owns a private jet, three mansions and a football club; he is extremely _____.
quests.explanation: A private jet, three mansions and a football club show enormous wealth, so rich fits.

quests.question: He bought a gold watch and a speedboat on his first pay cheque, spending _____.
quests.explanation: A gold watch and a speedboat from a first pay cheque show spending far beyond need: extravagantly.
